subject: Request: Temporary cache persistence exception in DPA redline (FinApps)
messages:
From: Olivia Ross <olivia.ross@finapps.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@finapps.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: DPA redline + short-lived cache persistence ask

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Marcus and I reviewed the DPA redline you sent and we have one practical ask that would affect our production design: FinApps relies on a short-lived encrypted cache of user prompts and model outputs for 48 hours to support a real-time analytics pipeline and customer troubleshooting. Our security team prefers not to maintain these logs long-term, but we need the temporary persistence window.

On your DPA v3 the section on "temporary storage for operational purposes" appears to disallow cached persistence beyond ephemeral memory. Can Redwood consider a narrow exception scoped to: (1) retention <= 48 hours, (2) AES-256 encrypted at rest, (3) access limited to support and on-call SREs with audit logging?

We're happy to accept a written addendum and some additional logging/audit commitments if that helps. Attaching our proposed redline (FinApps-redline-DPA-v3.pdf) with the highlighted clause.

Would you please route this to the right folks for product/security sign-off? We are aiming to close the contract next week.

—Olivia
Olivia Ross
Head of Product Security, FinApps

Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:40:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: DPA redline + short-lived cache persistence ask (FinApps)

Stephanie / all — thanks for the ping. High-level security response: the ask is reasonable if we can enforce these controls absolutely and get visibility/audit. Specific items we need before sign-off: 

- Precise definition of "cache": confirm whether the data will be stored on node-local ephemeral disks, a managed Redis cluster, or a separate encrypted object store. Each has different threat models.
- Key management: keys must be customer-specific or Redwood-managed with HSM/KMS and key-rotation logging. We should prefer customer KMS for higher assurance.
- Access policy: limit to a named support/SRE group, enforce MFA, require justification logging for any access.
- Audit trail: retention of access logs for 90 days and automated anomaly alerts for accesses outside normal windows.
- Data minimization: confirm they do not require PII or PHI to be stored in the cache; if they do, we need explicit handling and likely cannot accept in the same way.

If Product can provide the storage architecture and how RBAC/audit will be implemented, Security can draft the acceptance criteria. If we meet these, Legal can wrap into an addendum.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 13:12:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: DPA redline + short-lived cache persistence ask (FinApps)

Quick technical summary from Product/Infra after reviewing the note and our infra options: 

- Implementation options: (A) customer-dedicated in-memory encrypted Redis (preferred), (B) encrypted object store with lifecycle policy, (C) node-local ephemeral disk with encryption. 
- Cost/SLO: option A adds a modest monthly infra increment for a dedicated Redis instance pool and increases operational complexity (monitoring/backups). Latency impact is negligible. Option B increases token egress/storage billing and requires lifecycle hooks to enforce 48h TTL. Option C is the least operationally friendly for multi-tenant hosting.
- RBAC/audit: we can gate access via Service Account ACLs + Cloud IAM roles; audit logs already captured by our logging stack and can be retained for 90 days with existing retention tier.
- KMS: we support both customer-managed CMEK via AWS KMS and Redwood-managed keys via our HSM. Customer KMS would meet Security's preference.

Proposed mitigation bundle to present to FinApps: use option A (dedicated encrypted Redis), CMEK with customer KMS, strict IAM group limiting to on-call/support with MFA, 90-day audit retention, automated purge job ensuring TTL <= 48h, and a joint runbook for incident access requests.

If Legal wants precise phrasing, we can include a short operational addendum describing the technical controls. I can draft the design note (cache-persistence-design-note.pdf attached).

—Dev Patel
Principal Product Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
To: Olivia Ross <olivia.ross@finapps.com>, Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@finapps.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline + short-lived cache persistence ask

Olivia / Marcus — thanks for the patience. Internal alignment summary and proposal we can sign off on in principle: 

1) Scope: exception limited to non-PII/non-PHI inference payloads for operational troubleshooting and analytics, persisted for a maximum of 48 hours.
2) Controls (mandatory): dedicated encrypted Redis instance per account; customer-managed CMEK (preferred) or Redwood HSM if customer declines; IAM limited to named support/SRE group with MFA and justification logging; audit logs retained for 90 days; automated TTL enforcement and daily verification reports.
3) Legal: we will accept a one-paragraph addendum to the DPA that references the operational controls above and affirms the 48-hour cap. Redwood will require an initial security attestation and include a quarterly compliance check for this exception.

Next steps: Vivek, can Legal draft the one-paragraph addendum and a short statement of acceptance criteria we can attach to the MSA? Neha, please confirm any additional checks for the initial attestation. Dev, please prepare the design note and a quick runbook for access requests.

Olivia — if that matches your expectations we can provide the addendum and the design note for signature today and hope to get the countersigned DPA by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
